_meta.role: Practical Guidance Store - per-issue action steps and official portal definitions. Highest change-rate, lowest legal-risk file of the three; kept separate so editing steps/URLs can never corrupt verified legal text.
_meta.population_status: SKELETON - no guidance or portals populated. Populated per issue only after taxonomy sign-off.
governance: CLAUDE.md Section 8 (action-step and portal rules), Section 7.2 (why three files).

Action steps are issue-specific (never generic domain boilerplate), most time-sensitive first, max 5, no FIR filing as primary advice, no criminal procedure steps. Curated by humans - an LLM must not freely generate legally sensitive procedure steps at request time.
Portals: only official government / regulator / statutory-authority portals. Conditional portals (e.g. a banking ombudsman) must carry a usage_condition and must not be returned unconditionally.
Wording in action steps must follow CLAUDE.md Section 10 (no 'you will win', no 'definitely applies', etc.).
consumed_by: Module 3 (Legal Intelligence Engine): given the detected issue_id, reads action_steps; resolves portal_ids against 'portals'; filters portals to those whose supported_issue_ids contain the issue_id; sorts by priority (immediate -> primary -> secondary); returns max 3.
Module 4 (Response Builder): places the returned steps/portals into the response contract fields 'action_steps' and 'portals'.
knowledge_base_loader: loads and reference-validates this file at startup (read-only at runtime).

<issue_id>._id_rule: issue_id must exist in issue_mappings.json (same signed-off taxonomy).
action_steps: array of 1-5 strings - ordered, issue-specific steps; index 0 is the most time-sensitive. Plain language, awareness-safe wording.
portal_ids: array of strings - each must resolve to an entry in 'portals'. Order here is informational; Module 3's priority sort decides final order.

<portal_id>._id_rule: portal_id is a stable snake_case string, e.g. 'cybercrime_gov_in'.
<portal_id>.portal_id: string - MUST equal the object key. Explicit self-identifier so records are safe to validate, iterate, and pass around detached from their key.
<portal_id>.name: string - official portal name
<portal_id>.official_url: string | null - confirmed official URL only; null until confirmed, never a placeholder
<portal_id>.purpose: string - what a citizen uses this portal for
<portal_id>.priority: enum: 'immediate' (time-sensitive, contact within ~24h) | 'primary' (main formal complaint avenue) | 'secondary' (alternative/supplementary)
<portal_id>.usage_condition: string | null - REQUIRED (non-null) for conditional portals; describes when this portal applies (e.g. only after an initial complaint to the bank). null means unconditional for its supported issues.
<portal_id>.official_source: string - owning authority, e.g. 'Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India'
supported_issue_ids: array of strings - issue IDs this portal supports; Module 3 filters on membership here

action_steps: Contact your bank immediately and report the unauthorised transaction. Ask the bank to block the card, account, or UPI ID involved to prevent further loss.
Call the national cyber crime helpline 1930 as soon as possible - early reporting improves the chance of freezing the fraudulent transfer.
Preserve all evidence: the caller's number, SMS alerts, transaction IDs, screenshots, and the exact time of the calls and debits.
File a written complaint on the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal and keep the acknowledgment number for follow-up.
Follow up with your bank in writing about reversal or chargeback of the unauthorised transaction, and keep copies of every communication.
If any money was transferred because of the impersonation, contact your bank immediately and call the national cyber crime helpline 1930 to report the financial fraud.
Preserve evidence before it can be deleted: take screenshots of the fake profile or messages, and note the profile link, caller numbers, and dates and times.
Report the fake profile or account to the platform (social media site, messaging app, or website) using its impersonation reporting option and request its removal.
File a complaint on the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal with the collected evidence and keep the acknowledgment number for follow-up.
Inform the people being contacted in your name - a simple warning message prevents relatives, friends, or colleagues from being cheated.
If you entered any password, PIN, or card details on the suspicious page, change those passwords immediately and contact your bank to block the card or account before further misuse.
If any money was debited, call the national cyber crime helpline 1930 right away - early reporting improves the chance of freezing the fraudulent transfer.
Do not click the link again or forward it. Preserve evidence: screenshots of the message and page, the sender's number or email address, and the link itself.
File a complaint on the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal with the evidence and keep the acknowledgment number for follow-up.
Report the fraudulent SMS, call, or WhatsApp message on the Chakshu facility of Sanchar Saathi so the sender can be acted against.

cybercrime_gov_in.name: National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal
cybercrime_gov_in.purpose: File complaints about cybercrime incidents, including online financial fraud, and track their status.
cybercrime_gov_in.official_source: Ministry of Home Affairs (Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre), Government of India

rbi_cms.name: RBI Complaint Management System (Integrated Ombudsman Scheme)
rbi_cms.purpose: Escalate a complaint about an unauthorised banking transaction against a bank or regulated entity.
rbi_cms.usage_condition: Use only if you have already complained to your bank about the unauthorised transaction and it has not been resolved satisfactorily within the bank's stipulated time (typically 30 days).

sanchar_saathi_chakshu.name: Sanchar Saathi - Chakshu (Report Suspected Fraud Communication)
sanchar_saathi_chakshu.purpose: Report suspected fraud calls, SMS, or WhatsApp communications, including impersonation of officials, companies, or known persons.
sanchar_saathi_chakshu.usage_condition: Use when the fraudulent communication (impersonation, fake link, or fraud attempt) came through a phone call, SMS, or WhatsApp, in addition to filing the main complaint on the cyber crime portal.
sanchar_saathi_chakshu.official_source: Department of Telecommunications, Ministry of Communications, Government of India
